strings.ec.art.paris.title: Paris
strings.ec.art.paris.body: Paris is the capital of France, and the river Seine flows through it. Its best-known landmark, the Eiffel Tower, was completed in 1889. London lies to the north across the English Channel, and Madrid to the south-west. Lyon and Marseille are large French cities, but Paris is the capital.
strings.ec.art.london.title: London
strings.ec.art.london.body: London is the capital of the United Kingdom, and the River Thames flows through it. The Tower of London, a fortress beside the river, was begun about 1078 under William the Conqueror. Across the Irish Sea to the west lies Dublin, and across the Channel to the south, Paris. Manchester and Liverpool are big English cities, but London is the capital.
strings.ec.art.dublin.title: Dublin
strings.ec.art.dublin.body: Dublin is the capital of Ireland. It stands on the east coast, at the mouth of the River Liffey, facing the Irish Sea. Dublin has been the capital of independent Ireland since 1922, when the Irish Free State was created. Cork, in the south, is a big Irish city, but Dublin is the capital, and London is the capital of the neighbouring United Kingdom.
strings.ec.art.madrid.title: Madrid
strings.ec.art.madrid.body: Madrid is the capital of Spain. It lies almost in the exact centre of the country, far from the sea, and has been the permanent seat of the court since 1561. Barcelona, on the Mediterranean coast, is Spain's second-largest city and the capital of Catalonia, but it is not the national capital. To the west of Madrid lies Lisbon, the capital of Portugal.
strings.ec.art.lisbon.title: Lisbon
strings.ec.art.lisbon.body: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal. It stands on the estuary of the river Tagus, where the river widens before it reaches the Atlantic Ocean. A great earthquake destroyed much of the city in 1755. Porto, on the Douro in the north, is Portugal's second city but not its capital, and Madrid, the capital of Spain, lies to the east.
strings.ec.art.berlin.title: Berlin
strings.ec.art.berlin.body: Berlin is the capital of Germany, and the river Spree flows through it. The Brandenburg Gate, built by 1791, is its best-known landmark. The Berlin Wall, built in 1961, divided the city until it fell in 1989. Prague lies to the south of Berlin, and Vienna further to the south-east.
strings.ec.art.vienna.title: Vienna
strings.ec.art.vienna.body: Vienna (Wien in German, Beč in Croatian) is the capital of Austria, and the Danube flows through it. The Congress of Vienna, which redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon, met here in 1814-15. Salzburg, the birthplace of Mozart, is a famous Austrian city but not the capital. Budapest lies further down the Danube, to the east of Vienna.
strings.ec.art.prague.title: Prague
strings.ec.art.prague.body: Prague is the capital of Czechia. Its river is the Vltava (the Moldau in German), which flows on into the Elbe. Work on Charles Bridge, its famous bridge over the river, began in 1357. Berlin lies to the north of Prague and Vienna to the south-east.
strings.ec.art.budapest.title: Budapest
strings.ec.art.budapest.body: Budapest is the capital of Hungary, and the Danube flows through it. It was formed in 1873, when the towns of Buda, Óbuda and Pest on the two banks of the river were joined into one city. Vienna lies up the river, to the west. Do not mix it up with Bucharest, the capital of Romania.
strings.ec.art.zagreb.title: Zagreb
strings.ec.art.zagreb.body: Zagreb is the capital of Croatia, and the river Sava flows through it. It lies in the north-west of the country, close to Slovenia. Zagreb has been the capital of independent Croatia since 1991, when the country declared independence. Vienna lies to the north of Zagreb and Budapest to the north-east.
strings.ec.art.rome.title: Rome
strings.ec.art.rome.body: Rome is the capital of Italy, and the river Tiber (Tevere in Italian) flows through it. The Colosseum, its great amphitheatre, was completed in AD 80. Milan, in the north, is Italy's famous business and fashion city, but only Rome is the capital. South of Sicily lies the island country of Malta, whose capital is Valletta, while Athens lies across the sea to the east.
strings.ec.art.athens.title: Athens
strings.ec.art.athens.body: Athens is the capital of Greece, and it became the capital in 1834. The Parthenon, the temple on the Acropolis hill above the city, was substantially finished by 432 BC. The Colosseum in Rome was completed more than five centuries later, in AD 80, so the Greek temple is the older of the two. Athens is called Atena in Croatian.

strings.enc.h.h-west.s-west-thames.clue: A fortress beside the river was begun here under William the Conqueror. Find its page.
strings.enc.h.h-west.s-west-thames.name: The fortress key
strings.enc.h.h-west.s-west-lisbon.clue: My river widens before it reaches the Atlantic, and an earthquake once shook my streets. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-west.s-west-lisbon.name: The Atlantic compass
strings.enc.h.h-central.title: Capitals of the middle
strings.enc.h.h-central.intro: Rivers, bridges and walls: the capitals of Central Europe are waiting.
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-vienna.clue: Here a congress redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-vienna.name: The congress seal
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-wall.clue: A wall once divided my city in two. Find my page and learn when it fell.
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-wall.name: The brick of the wall
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-budapest.clue: Three towns on two river banks became one city. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-budapest.name: The brass bridge
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-prague.clue: My famous bridge over the Vltava was begun in 1357. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-central.s-cen-prague.name: The stone bridge key
strings.enc.h.h-south.title: Capitals of the south
strings.enc.h.h-south.intro: Marble, temples and old stones: the southern capitals are the oldest of all.
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-rome.clue: A great amphitheatre stands in my capital, beside the Tiber. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-rome.name: The gladiator coin
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-athens.clue: A temple crowns the hill above my city. Find my page.
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-athens.name: The olive branch
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-oldest.clue: A Greek temple is older than a Roman arena. Read on and find which landmark is the oldest.
strings.enc.h.h-south.s-south-oldest.name: The marble column
